subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me a challenging GCSE exam-style question on organic chemistry, then mark my answer against the spec.
promptWeak: Explain organic chemistry for GCSE simply, with a worked example and the most common mistake.
learningObjectives: Fuels and petroleum: fractional distillation of crude oil
Homologous series, functional groups and general formulae
Alkanes: saturated hydrocarbons and substitution reactions
Alkenes: unsaturation, the bromine-water test and addition reactions
Alcohols and the production of ethanol

questions.lo: Fuels and petroleum: fractional distillation of crude oil
questions.q: Crude oil is separated into useful fractions by which process?
questions.explain: Crude oil is separated by fractional distillation, which relies on the different boiling points of the fractions.

questions.lo: Fuels and petroleum: fractional distillation of crude oil
questions.q: In a fractionating column, where are the fractions with the LOWEST boiling points collected?
options: At the top, where it is coolest
They are not collected at all
At the bottom, where it is hottest
questions.explain: The column is hottest at the bottom. Fractions with the lowest boiling points (smallest molecules) rise highest and are collected at the cooler top of the column.

questions.lo: Fuels and petroleum: fractional distillation of crude oil
questions.q: Which fraction is used as fuel for cars?
questions.explain: Petrol (gasoline) is the fraction used as fuel for cars. Bitumen is used for roads and refinery gases for bottled gas.

questions.lo: Homologous series, functional groups and general formulae
questions.q: What is the general formula of the alkanes?
questions.explain: Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons with the general formula CnH2n+2.

questions.lo: Homologous series, functional groups and general formulae
questions.q: Which of these is a feature of a homologous series?
options: Members have completely different chemical properties
questions.explain: In a homologous series, consecutive members differ by a CH2 unit, share the same general formula and functional group, and have similar chemical properties.

questions.lo: Alkanes: saturated hydrocarbons and substitution reactions
questions.q: Why are alkanes described as saturated?
options: They contain a carbon-carbon double bond
They contain only single carbon-carbon bonds
questions.explain: Alkanes are saturated because they contain only single carbon-carbon bonds, with the maximum number of hydrogen atoms.

questions.lo: Alkanes: saturated hydrocarbons and substitution reactions
questions.q: Methane reacts with chlorine in the presence of UV light. What type of reaction is this?
questions.explain: Alkanes react with chlorine in UV light by substitution, where a hydrogen atom is replaced by a chlorine atom (e.g. forming chloromethane and hydrogen chloride).

questions.lo: Alkenes: unsaturation, the bromine-water test and addition reactions
questions.q: What structural feature makes an alkene unsaturated?
questions.explain: Alkenes are unsaturated because they contain a carbon-carbon double bond (C=C).

questions.lo: Alkenes: unsaturation, the bromine-water test and addition reactions
questions.q: A gas is bubbled through orange bromine water and the colour disappears. What does this show?
options: The gas is an unsaturated alkene
The gas is a saturated alkane
questions.explain: Alkenes decolourise bromine water (orange to colourless) because the C=C double bond undergoes an addition reaction. Alkanes do not.

questions.lo: Alkenes: unsaturation, the bromine-water test and addition reactions
questions.q: When ethene reacts with bromine, what is the product?
questions.explain: Ethene undergoes an addition reaction with bromine to form 1,2-dibromoethane, with the double bond opening up.

questions.lo: Alcohols and the production of ethanol
questions.q: What is the functional group of the alcohols?
questions.explain: Alcohols contain the hydroxyl functional group, -OH.

questions.lo: Alcohols and the production of ethanol
questions.q: In the fermentation of glucose to make ethanol, which conditions and catalyst are used?
options: Yeast at around 25-35 C in the absence of air
questions.explain: Fermentation uses yeast (which provides enzymes) at about 25-35 C in the absence of air, converting glucose into ethanol and carbon dioxide.

questions.lo: Alcohols and the production of ethanol
questions.q: Ethanol can also be made by the catalytic addition of steam to ethene. Which catalyst is used?
questions.explain: Ethene reacts with steam using a phosphoric acid catalyst to form ethanol (hydration/catalytic addition).

questions.lo: Carboxylic acids and esters
questions.q: What is the functional group of a carboxylic acid?
questions.explain: Carboxylic acids contain the carboxyl functional group, -COOH.

questions.lo: Carboxylic acids and esters
questions.q: An ester is formed by reacting a carboxylic acid with which type of compound?
questions.explain: Esters are made by reacting a carboxylic acid with an alcohol (usually with an acid catalyst).

questions.lo: Carboxylic acids and esters
questions.q: Ethanoic acid reacts with a reactive metal such as magnesium to give a salt and which gas?
questions.explain: Like other acids, carboxylic acids react with reactive metals to produce a salt and hydrogen gas.

questions.lo: Addition and condensation polymers
questions.q: Poly(ethene) is made from ethene monomers. What type of polymerisation is this?
questions.explain: Poly(ethene) is formed by addition polymerisation, where many ethene monomers (with C=C bonds) join with no other product formed.

questions.lo: Addition and condensation polymers
questions.q: Which statement about condensation polymerisation is correct?
options: Only one type of monomer with a C=C bond is used
A small molecule such as water is lost when monomers join
questions.explain: In condensation polymerisation, monomers with two functional groups join and a small molecule (such as water) is released each time a bond forms.

questions.lo: Structural formulae and isomerism
questions.q: What are structural isomers?
options: Compounds with the same molecular formula but different structural formulae
questions.explain: Structural isomers have the same molecular formula but different arrangements of atoms (different structural formulae).

questions.lo: Structural formulae and isomerism
questions.q: Which pair are structural isomers of one another (both C4H10)?
questions.explain: Butane and methylpropane both have the molecular formula C4H10 but different structures, so they are structural isomers. But-1-ene is C4H8, so it is not an isomer of butane.
